name: SchoolTracs Public API
description:
The Public API lets your own software talk to SchoolTracs directly: pull tomorrow's
timetable into a display screen, push a web enquiry form straight into your leads, mark
attendance from a tablet app, or sync invoices into your accounting system.

Everything is JSON over HTTPS. There are no SDKs to install — an API key and an HTTP
client are enough.

## Getting started

1. In SchoolTracs, open **Settings → Integration → API access** and create a key. You can
   hold up to 5 live keys at a time.
2. Send that key as an `X-Api-Key` header on every request.
3. Start with `GET /v1/centers` — it is the cheapest call that proves your key works and
   tells you which centre IDs you are allowed to touch.

```bash
curl https://web.schooltracs.com/v4/api/v1/centers \
  -H "X-Api-Key: YOUR_KEY_HERE"
```

## How a key decides what you can see

A key is bound to one organisation and one centre when it is created, and that binding
cannot be overridden by anything you put in a request. Every query is silently narrowed to
the centres your key covers. Asking for a record that belongs to someone else returns
**404**, not 403 — the API will not confirm that a record exists outside your own data.

You can omit `centerId`, including when creating records; it defaults to your API key's
centre. If you supply `centerId`, it must match that centre.

## What comes back

A single record:

```json
{
  "data": { "id": 9101, "name": "Amelia Tsang" },
  "meta": { "message": "OK", "apiVersion": "v1", "timestamp": "2026-03-14T09:20:11+00:00" }
}
```

A list adds paging information to `meta` — and note that a list response carries **no**
`message` key, only single-record responses do:

```json
{
  "data": [ { "id": 9101, "name": "Amelia Tsang" } ],
  "meta": {
    "currentPage": 1, "from": 1, "lastPage": 6, "perPage": 50, "to": 50, "total": 284,
    "links": {
      "first": "https://web.schooltracs.com/v4/api/v1/customers?page=1",
      "last":  "https://web.schooltracs.com/v4/api/v1/customers?page=6",
      "prev":  null,
      "next":  "https://web.schooltracs.com/v4/api/v1/customers?page=2"
    },
    "apiVersion": "v1",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-14T09:20:11+00:00"
  }
}
```

The simplest way to walk a whole list is to follow `meta.links.next` until it is `null`,
rather than counting pages yourself. `lastPage` and the `last`/`next` links respect your
plan's page-depth limit. `total` counts all matching records, including those beyond the
pages your plan allows.

## Dates and times

Calendar dates use `YYYY-MM-DD`, for example `2026-03-17`, with no time or timezone.
Use this format for date filters too, including filters on timestamp fields such as
`filter[created][gte]=2026-03-17`: those filters compare calendar dates.

Response timestamps such as `created`, `updated`, `attendanceUpdated`, `postedDate` and
`meta.timestamp` use ISO 8601: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss±HH:mm`, for example
`2026-03-17T08:31:02+00:00`. The offset identifies the timezone; `+00:00` means UTC.
Use the supplied offset when converting a timestamp to your local time.

Lesson `startTime` and `endTime` are timetable times without a timezone offset, paired
with the lesson's `date`. They use `HH:mm` or `HH:mm:ss`, for example `16:30` or
`16:30:00` (4:30 pm). Both forms are accepted when creating or updating a lesson;
responses return the stored value. For a lesson ending after midnight, `endTime` can
have an hour of 24 or more: `25:30:00` means 1:30 am on the day after `date`.
When creating a lesson, the latest permitted end time is `32:00` or `32:00:00`
(8:00 am on the next day); any later value is rejected.
Minutes and seconds must be `00`–`59`, and `startTime` hours must be `00`–`23`.
Malformed time components such as `31:60` are rejected with `422` on create and update.

The webhook `SchoolTracs-Timestamp` header uses a different representation: an integer
number of seconds since `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` (Unix time), not milliseconds.

## Shaping a query

Every list endpoint accepts the same four tools. The exact field names each one accepts
are listed on the endpoint itself.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `filter[field]=value` | Narrow the result set. Operators like `[gte]`, `[in]` and `[exists]` are described per field. |
| `sort=-created,name` | Order the results. A leading `-` sorts descending; list several fields comma separated. |
| `fields[table]=id,name` | Return only the fields you need. `id` always comes back. The key is the model's table name, so it is `fields[customer]`, `fields[activity]`, `fields[order_item]`. |
| `include=customer,receipts` | Embed related records instead of making a second call. |

Three filter behaviours are worth knowing up front, because they are not guessable:

- **`exists` asks about null, not about truth.** `filter[email][exists]=true` means "has an
  email address on file"; `false` means the field is empty. It accepts `1/true/yes/on` and
  `0/false/no/off/null`.
- **JSON values are accepted anywhere a bracket would be.** `filter[created]={"gte":"2026-01-01"}`
  does the same thing as `filter[created][gte]=2026-01-01`. Useful when your HTTP client
  makes nested query keys awkward.
- **Exact-match fields can reach through a relation.** `filter[customer.email]=…` works on
  endpoints whose `customer` is an exact-match field, and an explicit `null` means "is unset".

## Deleted, refunded and reversed records

By default you see live records only. `?withTrashed=true` adds soft-deleted ones and
`?onlyTrashed=true` returns just those — both on the PAID plan only; a FREE key gets the
ordinary result set back instead of an error.

For money records, "deleted" is not the same thing as "undone":

- an **order item** is refunded by reducing its own quantity and total, so the row is still
  there — use `filter[refunded]=true` to see those;
- a **receipt** is reversed by a later receipt pointing back at it, and the original row is
  never deleted — use `filter[reversed]=true`.

## FREE and PAID plans

Your plan is a property of the centre, not of the key. It changes the limits, and on some
resources it changes what comes back at all.

| Limit | FREE | PAID |
|---|---|---|
| Live API keys | 5 | 5 |
| Requests per minute | 20 | 120 |
| Requests per day | 500 | 5,000 |
| Requests per month | 2,500 | 150,000 |
| Write requests per minute | no separate budget — writes come out of the overall limit | 60 |
| Requests per minute across all your keys | — | 1,200 |
| Requests in flight at once | 1 | 5 |
| Largest page | 50 | 500 |
| Pages you can reach | 5 | 200 |
| Scopes | `read:*`, `write:customers`, `write:leads` | `read:*`, `write:*`, `webhook:*` |

On top of those, **historical pulls are capped at 5 per minute on every plan**. A request
counts as a historical pull when you page past page 3, or when a date filter is open-ended
or spans more than 90 days. If you are backfilling, pace it.

What a FREE key cannot do:

- **Write most things.** A FREE key can write `customers` and `leads` — enough to push
  registrations and web enquiries in — but nothing else. Every other POST and PATCH is
  rejected with `403` before it reaches a controller.
- **Read invoices, receipts, order items or journal entries.** Those four resources refuse
  a FREE key outright.
- **See the full customer record.** `GET /v1/customers` returns 16 fields on FREE instead of
  the full set — the extra ones are simply absent rather than null. Each PAID-only field is
  marked in the schema below.
- **Look far back.** Lessons are limited to a rolling window of today ±6 days, and
  enrolments to currently-active ones. On PAID those become real date-range queries, still
  bounded: at most 3 years back and 1 year wide per request.

## Webhooks

Four resources can push a change to your own server the moment it happens, instead of you
polling for it: **students, orders, invoices and receipts**. Nothing else in this API fires a
webhook — lessons, courses, fees, staff and journal notes don't, however you change them.

### Setting one up

There's no REST endpoint for this. Subscribe from **Settings → Integration → API access**, in
the **Webhook** section: pick a `https://` delivery URL and turn on the entity-level events you
want (`student.*`, `order.*`, `invoice.*`, `receipt.*`). SchoolTracs generates the signing
secret when you save the subscription and shows it to you there, so you can have your
verification in place before the first delivery arrives. Webhooks need the `webhook:*` scope,
which only exists on the PAID plan — the option is unavailable on FREE.

Deliveries fire for a change made **anywhere** in SchoolTracs — the staff app, checkout, an
import — not only for writes made through this API. An enrolment write here, for instance,
creates or updates the underlying course order and can trigger an `order.*` delivery even
though there is no direct "orders" write endpoint in this API.

### What you receive

A `POST` to your delivery URL, with a body shaped like this:

```json
{
  "id": "3f9d2e0a-1b2c-4d5e-8f6a-7b8c9d0e1f23",
  "event": "invoice.paid",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "created": "2026-03-18T01:05:11+00:00",
  "data": { "object": { "...": "the same shape GET /v1/invoices/{id} returns" } }
}
```

`data.object` is the resource **re-read at delivery time**, not a diff of what changed or a
snapshot of the moment the event fired. One behaviour worth knowing before you rely on it: it
is built without any `?include=`, so a field that would normally only appear when you ask for
it — `customer`, `center`, `receipt`, and the like — comes back as an **empty object `{}`**
rather than being left out of the payload the way a REST response leaves it out. Treat `{}` as
"not sent", not as "this relation is empty" — re-fetch the record over REST if you need it.

### Events

| Entity | Events |
|---|---|
| `student` | `created`, `updated`, `deleted` |
| `order` | `created`, `updated`, `deleted` |
| `invoice` | `issued` (created), `updated`, `voided` (deleted), `paid` |
| `receipt` | `created`, `updated`, `deleted` |

`invoice.paid` fires the moment `paid` first reaches `total` — not on every save of an
already-settled invoice, and not on a partial payment that doesn't clear the balance. It can
arrive **alongside** `invoice.updated` for the same write, if that write both changes something
else and clears the balance — don't assume one write means one delivery.

Subscribing to an entity's `*` wildcard (`invoice.*`, and so on) covers every event for that
entity in one subscription, rather than wiring each one up separately.

### Verifying a delivery

Every request carries:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SchoolTracs-Event` | The event name, e.g. `invoice.paid`. |
| `SchoolTracs-Delivery` | A UUID unique to this delivery — use it to de-duplicate retries. |
| `SchoolTracs-Timestamp` | Unix timestamp, in seconds, matching what was signed. |
| `X-Signature` | `v1=<hex-encoded HMAC>` — `HMAC-SHA256("{timestamp}.{raw body}", your signing secret)`. Recompute it and compare before trusting a payload. |

Your delivery URL must be `https://` and publicly resolvable — `localhost`, `.local` hostnames,
and private or reserved IP ranges are all rejected when you save the subscription.

### Retries and debouncing

A non-2xx response, or a network failure, counts as a failed delivery: it is retried roughly
every 5 minutes for up to 24 hours, then given up on. **Every** attempt — successful or not —
is logged and visible under **Settings → Logs → Webhook**, including the request that was sent
and the response or error that came back.

Several saves to the same record within a 5-second window collapse into a single delivery of
the final state, rather than one per save — so don't assume one API write produces one webhook
call.

## When something goes wrong

Controllers return this shape:

```json
{ "status": "error", "message": "Validation failed.", "errors": { "name": ["The name field is required."] } }
```

Auth and rate limiting run *before* any controller, so those failures are shorter — just
`{"message": "…"}`, with no `status` or `errors` key. Handle both.

| Status | What happened |
|---|---|
| `400` | The request was understood but the operation is not allowed right now — the message explains. |
| `401` | Missing, unknown or revoked `X-Api-Key`. |
| `403` | Your plan does not include this endpoint, or the record belongs to a centre your key cannot write to. |
| `404` | No such record — including records that exist but belong to another centre. |
| `409` | A sales action wants confirmation first. Re-send with `confirmed`. |
| `422` | Validation failed, or you exceeded a plan limit on page size, page depth or date range. |
| `429` | A rate limit ran out. `window` says which one and `retry_after` says for how long. |
| `500` | Something broke on our side. The message is deliberately generic; the details are in our logs. |

Two limits return `422` rather than quietly doing something else: asking for a page size
above your plan's ceiling, and paging deeper than your plan allows. Neither is clamped.

## There is no delete endpoint

Nothing in this API deletes a record. There is no `DELETE` verb on any resource, by design,
and no write scope grants deletion — not even `write:*`. The nearest equivalents are two
explicit, named actions that do the right bookkeeping either side of the record they close
out: `POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/cancel` and `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/void`.

Trying to reach deletion through a field does not work either. Sending `deleted` or
`deletedAt` as a truthy value in the body of **any** write is rejected outright with a
`403` before the request reaches the endpoint — it is not quietly dropped, and it will not
take a record down.

Invoices are also not creatable. They are produced as a side effect of ordering and
checkout, so the API exposes only a due-date change and a void.

Nothing in this API deletes a record. There is no `DELETE` verb on any resource, by design,
and no write scope grants deletion — not even `write:*`. The nearest equivalents are two
explicit, named actions that do the right bookkeeping either side of the record they close
out: `POST /v1/enrollments/{id}/cancel` and `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/void`.

Trying to reach deletion through a field does not work either. Sending `deleted` or
`deletedAt` as a truthy value in the body of **any** write is rejected outright with a
`403` before the request reaches the endpoint — it is not quietly dropped, and it will not
take a record down.

Invoices are also not creatable. They are produced as a side effect of ordering and
checkout, so the API exposes only a due-date change and a void.
